title: Palindrome Number
summary: Determine if an integer x is a palindrome by comparing it with its reversed version.
statement: Determine if an integer x is a palindrome by comparing it with its reversed version.
constraints: Negative integers are not palindromes because the minus sign is not mirrored.
hints: Negative values and nonzero trailing-zero values can be rejected immediately.
Reverse only the last half of the digits and compare it with the first half.
Move last digits into a reversed half until it meets the remaining first half; compare, ignoring one middle digit for odd length.
Reversing only half the number also avoids whole-number reversal overflow.
editorial: Reject negatives and positive numbers ending in zero. Repeatedly move the final digit into a reversed accumulator until the remaining prefix is no larger than that accumulator. For even length, the halves must match exactly. For odd length, discard the accumulator's middle digit before comparing. Zero is a palindrome.

tests.explanation: The decimal digits read 121 in both directions.
The minus sign is only at the beginning, so a negative number is not a palindrome.
